draft.title: Comparing sources to check accuracy
card: Historians often check one source against another. This is called corroboration, which means finding support for a claim from a second source.
If two sources were made independently, each one's claim is more likely to be accurate when they agree. Independent means the makers did not copy from each other or share the same origin.
Agreement does not prove a claim is true. If one source copied the other, the agreement counts for little, because it is really one account.
When sources disagree, the historian looks for why. The writers may have had different views, purposes, times or places, or one may have made a mistake.
draft.remember: Independent sources that agree support each other. When they disagree, ask why.

a.q: Two sources made independently both say a town's walls were built in 1200. What does this suggest about the claim?
opts: It is more likely to be accurate
It is proven beyond any doubt
It is less likely to be accurate
It tells us nothing about accuracy
a.why: Two independent sources that agree support each other, so the claim is more likely to be accurate. It is not proven beyond doubt, because agreement raises the chance of accuracy but does not guarantee it.
a.clue: Agreement between independent sources adds support.

b.q: Historian Priya finds two accounts of a battle that agree closely. Which finding would most weaken the value of that agreement?
opts: The later writer copied from the earlier one
The two writers lived in different towns
The accounts were written in different years
The two writers had never met each other
b.why: If one writer copied the other, the two accounts are really one source, so agreement adds little support. Different towns, different years and never meeting suggest the accounts were independent, which would keep the agreement useful.
b.clue: Ask whether the two accounts are truly separate.

a.best: It is more likely to be accurate

b.best: The later writer copied from the earlier one

problems.detail: The clue 'Agreement between independent sources adds support' nearly restates the right option, so a student can pick it without understanding the idea.
